short: A decade that destroyed the French monarchy and rewrote European politics.
full:
The storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789 followed months of fiscal crisis and the calling of the Estates-General for the first time since 1614. Within weeks feudal privileges were abolished and the Declaration of the Rights of Man adopted.

What followed was neither linear nor bloodless: constitutional monarchy, war with most of Europe, the execution of Louis XVI in 1793, and the Terror, in which perhaps 17,000 were guillotined. The Directory that emerged was unstable enough for Napoleon Bonaparte to overturn it in the coup of 18 Brumaire, November 1799. The Revolution's vocabulary — citizenship, nation, left and right, the rights of man — became the vocabulary of modern politics everywhere.
